verdict.rationale: Aqua's official trivy-mcp plugin advertises "Natural Language Scanning" and runs an MCP server that brings Trivy's scanning into VS Code and other MCP-enabled tools, so users can drive scans with natural-language questions. That capability is only reachable through a separate plugin and an external MCP-enabled AI client, and the evidence is a short feature claim with no detail on which commands or workflows it covers. Missing for 10: natural language built into the core CLI without an external AI client, documentation of which operations can be driven by natural language, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: Natural Language Scanning: Ask questions about security issues in natural language
This plugin starts a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that integrates Trivy's security scanning capabilities with VS Code and other MCP-enabled tools.
